signal: Today’s strongest signal is that frontier AI capability is increasingly being shaped by the runtime around the model: safeguarded model tiers, live containment and monitoring, database-style context planning, fine-grained MoE execution, and causal evaluation of retrieved skills are all becoming first-class engineering concerns.

stories.title: Anthropic releases Claude Fable 5.1 and Mythos 5.1 for long-running coding, research, and agent work
stories.summary: Anthropic released Claude Fable 5.1 as its most capable generally available model and Claude Mythos 5.1 as the same underlying model with reduced safeguards for vetted cybersecurity and life-sciences users. Anthropic reports 52.6% on Terminal-Bench-Science 0.1 and 55.8% on Terminal-Bench 4.0 for Fable 5.1, while Mythos 5.1 reaches 60.9% on Terminal-Bench 4.0. Cache-read pricing falls 75% to $0.25 per million tokens, which Anthropic estimates reduces typical Fable workloads by about 25% and highly agentic workloads by up to roughly 45%.
stories.whyItMatters: The model release matters as much for economics and deployment architecture as for raw benchmarks. Long-running agents repeatedly reread repository state, tool results, and durable instructions, so cache pricing can materially change total cost per completed task. Anthropic is also separating one underlying capability level into differently safeguarded product surfaces, reinforcing a useful design pattern: capability, authority, and access policy do not have to be bundled into one model endpoint.
stories.attention: Very high — frontier capability and cache economics are improving together for long-running agents

stories.title: OpenAI designates Astra its first Critical cybersecurity-capability model
stories.summary: OpenAI says Astra has crossed the Critical cybersecurity threshold in its Preparedness Framework: with the right tools and access it can discover previously unknown vulnerabilities and develop exploit chains against hardened systems without step-by-step human guidance. In internal evaluations, Astra found and used two zero-day vulnerabilities in an exploit chain, while OpenAI says it has added stronger model refusals, cross-conversation monitoring, production misalignment classifiers, and controls that can stop unauthorized activity before broader release.
stories.whyItMatters: This moves containment from a safety add-on to a release prerequisite for frontier agents. The relevant software architecture is layered: model alignment, tool and network isolation, user-risk classification, runtime action monitoring, automatic stop mechanisms, and restricted access to the most powerful workflows. As agents become capable of consequential multi-step actions, the runtime must be able to bound authority even when the underlying model could do much more.
stories.attention: Very high — critical cyber capability now requires runtime containment as a release prerequisite

stories.title: ContextPipe treats long-horizon agent context like a database query plan
stories.summary: ContextPipe reframes agent context assembly as a database-style execution problem. Its five-phase Plan-Bind-Optimize-Execute-Feedback pipeline uses a structured data-source catalog, a deterministic cache-aware optimizer, and EXPLAIN ANALYZE-style traces to decide what enters each prompt, in what order, and when history should be compacted. In a preliminary SWE-bench Pro Qutebrowser evaluation, the authors report 31% fewer total tokens, 23% fewer LLM calls, and 9% lower response time than append-only context construction, though with a lower KV-cache hit ratio.
stories.whyItMatters: Context engineering is usually hidden inside prompt builders and ad hoc compaction code, which makes long-running agents difficult to debug or reproduce. A query-planner abstraction makes context selection inspectable, replayable, and optimizable under explicit token and cache budgets. For production coding and research agents, that creates a clean systems boundary between the model and the runtime deciding what the model is allowed to see each turn.
stories.attention: High — context assembly is becoming a database-style execution problem

stories.title: PCoMoE moves MoE inference from whole experts to fine-grained path composition
stories.summary: PCoMoE argues that treating each Mixture-of-Experts expert as an indivisible execution unit leaves useful intra-expert redundancy untouched. The system decomposes expert computation into reusable paths, prunes low-value path combinations with layer-wise compatibility signals, and executes the remaining sub-expert structure through a hardware-oriented runtime. The authors report up to 1.31× end-to-end inference speedup while also improving accuracy by as much as 10% in their experiments.
stories.whyItMatters: Modern MoE serving stacks spend enormous effort routing, loading, and balancing experts, but the whole-expert abstraction may be too coarse. If useful computation can be composed and reused below the expert boundary, schedulers gain another axis for reducing memory traffic and wasted FLOPs. This is a reminder that the model’s logical architecture does not have to be the final systems-level execution granularity.
stories.attention: High — MoE inference is moving below whole-expert scheduling

stories.title: Skill Following shows aggregate retrieval gains can hide harmful skill use
stories.summary: A new EMNLP 2026 Findings paper evaluates 17 LLMs on coding and mathematics and asks a narrower question than ordinary retrieval benchmarks: when an agent actually retrieves a skill, does using that skill improve the same task? Its Retrieval-Invoked Actual-Use Effect compares matched skill-enabled and skill-disabled executions. The authors find an evaluation paradox: several models show positive aggregate retrieval lift while producing negative actual-use effects on the exact tasks where a skill was retrieved.
stories.whyItMatters: Agent skill libraries are growing quickly, but retrieval rate or overall benchmark improvement does not prove the model follows a retrieved procedure correctly. Teams should measure skill selection and skill execution counterfactually on the same tasks, otherwise a retriever can look successful merely because it activates on easier cases. This is especially important for coding agents where a wrong skill can confidently steer a long trajectory in the wrong direction.
stories.attention: High — retrieved skills need causal actual-use evaluation, not aggregate lift

takeaway: Engineer the AI layer so model capability is never the only control surface. Separate capability from authority, make context construction explicit and auditable, benchmark inference below the abstractions exposed by the model, and evaluate retrieved skills on the exact tasks where they are invoked. The durable advantage is increasingly the runtime that decides what the model sees, what it can do, how much compute it gets, and whether each intervention actually helps.
